citation: Thiede, K. W., Brendefur, J. L., Carney, M. B., Champion, J., Turner, L., Stewart, R., & Osguthorpe, R. D. (2018). Improving the accuracy of teachers' judgments of student learning. Teaching and Teacher Education, 76, 106-115. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tate.2018.08.004
report_number: Teaching and Teacher Education, 76, 106-115 (peer-reviewed journal article; underlying RCT = Boise State 'Developing Mathematical Thinking' (DMT) grant-funded project)
design: Cluster RCT; assignment level = School (two matched sets of 4 schools per year, replicated over 3 academic years); subject = mathematics; teachers from grades K-5, but student-achievement analysis restricted to Grades 2-5 (MAP administered only from Grade 2). 2 (FA: yes/no) x 2 (DMT: yes/no) FACTORIAL design -> four conditions: Control (business-as-usual), FA (formative-assessment PD), DMT (student-centered math instruction PD), DMT+FA (both). 267 teachers total (Control 65, FA 60, DMT 77, DMT+FA 65); achievement (Grades 2-5) subsample = 44 Control, 42 FA, 53 DMT, 45 DMT+FA teachers. Student math achievement measured with MAP (NWEA Measures of Academic Progress), a standardized district test, fall (pre) and spring (post); analyzed via multilevel regression with students nested in teacher (class), controlling for student pretest.
problems: NO standardizing SD is reported anywhere in the paper, so Hedges' g CANNOT be computed from this report alone; g is left null for all three arms. The paper reports MAP achievement as (a) Table 4 adjusted (pretest-controlled) posttest group MEANS with the standard ERROR of the mean in parentheses (NOT SDs), and (b) Table 5 multilevel-regression FACTORIAL coefficients (B, SE) in raw MAP/RIT points. No posttest SD, no pooled SD, no residual SD/MSE, no variance components, and no ICC are given (the only dispersion fact is that sample MAP scores 'ranged from 135 to 270'). Per the extraction spec I did NOT guess/invent an SD (e.g. the published NWEA MAP grade-2-5 RIT SD of ~14-16) -- this must be supplied centrally to standardize. IMPACT ESTIMATES recorded are raw MAP-point, pretest-adjusted, cluster(multilevel)-aware: for FA and DMT they equal the Table 5 main-effect coefficients (FA B=0.68 SE=0.60; DMT B=1.55 SE=2.72z, SE=0.57) and also match the Table 4 adjusted-mean minus Control differences. DESIGN CAVEAT: this is a 2x2 FACTORIAL, so the Table 5 'DMT' and 'FA' coefficients are MAIN EFFECTS (averaged over the other factor), not pure single-arm-vs-control contrasts; the cleanest arm-vs-control contrasts are the Table 4 adjusted-mean differences (FA-Control=0.67, DMT-Control=1.54, DMT+FA-Control=2.63), which I used as impact_estimate. The DMT+FA-vs-Control contrast (=DMT+FA+interaction coefficients, 1.55+0.68+0.41=2.64) has NO directly reported SE, so its impact_se is null. n_t/n_c are teacher/cluster counts for the Grades 2-5 achievement sample; student-level N is not reported. The MAP outcome is the only student-achievement outcome; teacher judgment-accuracy outcomes (absolute/relative accuracy, Tables 2-3, Figs 1-2) and the mediation model are intentionally skipped per task.

effect_sizes.arm_label: FA = formative-assessment PD (vs business-as-usual Control); 2x2 factorial main effect of FA
effect_sizes.timepoint: post (spring; end of academic year, pretest = fall same year)
effect_sizes.g_method: NOT COMPUTABLE from report: no standardizing SD reported. impact_estimate = Table 4 adjusted (pretest-controlled) posttest MAP mean difference FA - Control = 213.98 - 213.31 = 0.67 RIT points (matches Table 5 multilevel-regression FA main-effect coefficient B=0.68, SE=0.60, z=1.13, ns). To get g, divide by a posttest MAP/RIT SD supplied centrally (none in paper).
effect_sizes.page_ref: p.112 Table 4 (means); p.113 Table 5 (regression coefficients); p.111-112 sec 3.3 (n's)
effect_sizes.notes: FA main effect / FA-vs-Control contrast was non-significant (z=1.13, p>.05). n_t=42 FA teachers, n_c=44 Control teachers (Grades 2-5 achievement subsample); n_clusters=42+44=86. Table-4 SE of adjusted mean: FA .43, Control .42 (these are SEs, not SDs). Student-level N not reported.

effect_sizes.arm_label: DMT = student-centered mathematics instruction PD (Developing Mathematical Thinking) (vs business-as-usual Control); 2x2 factorial main effect of DMT
effect_sizes.timepoint: post (spring; end of academic year, pretest = fall same year)
effect_sizes.g_method: NOT COMPUTABLE from report: no standardizing SD reported. impact_estimate = Table 4 adjusted (pretest-controlled) posttest MAP mean difference DMT - Control = 214.85 - 213.31 = 1.54 RIT points (matches Table 5 multilevel-regression DMT main-effect coefficient B=1.55, SE=0.57, z=2.72, p<.01). To get g, divide by a posttest MAP/RIT SD supplied centrally (none in paper).
effect_sizes.page_ref: p.112 Table 4 (means); p.113 Table 5 (regression coefficients); p.111-112 sec 3.3 (n's)
effect_sizes.notes: DMT was the ONLY condition significantly related to higher student math achievement (Table 5 B=1.55, SE=0.57, z=2.72, p<.01). n_t=53 DMT teachers, n_c=44 Control teachers (Grades 2-5 achievement subsample); n_clusters=53+44=97. Table-4 SE of adjusted mean: DMT .38, Control .42. Student-level N not reported.

effect_sizes.arm_label: DMT+FA = student-centered math instruction PD plus formative-assessment PD (both) (vs business-as-usual Control)
effect_sizes.timepoint: post (spring; end of academic year, pretest = fall same year)
effect_sizes.g_method: NOT COMPUTABLE from report: no standardizing SD reported. impact_estimate = Table 4 adjusted (pretest-controlled) posttest MAP mean difference DMT+FA - Control = 215.94 - 213.31 = 2.63 RIT points (consistent with Table 5 sum of factorial coefficients DMT+FA+interaction = 1.55+0.68+0.41 = 2.64). The combined contrast's SE is NOT directly reported (Table 5 gives only individual coefficient SEs: DMT .57, FA .60, DMTxFA .82), so impact_se is null. To get g, divide by a posttest MAP/RIT SD supplied centrally (none in paper).
effect_sizes.page_ref: p.112 Table 4 (means); p.113 Table 5 (regression coefficients); p.111-112 sec 3.3 (n's)
effect_sizes.notes: DMT+FA had the highest adjusted mean (215.94). The DMTxFA interaction was non-significant (Table 5 B=0.41, SE=0.82, z=0.50), so the combined condition's effect is approximately additive. impact_se left null because the combined arm-vs-control contrast SE is not reported (would require the model's coefficient covariances). n_t=45 DMT+FA teachers, n_c=44 Control teachers (Grades 2-5 achievement subsample); n_clusters=45+44=89. Table-4 SE of adjusted mean: DMT+FA .41, Control .42. Student-level N not reported.
